sources.title: The Free Firearm Sound Library
sources.evidence: The OpenGameArt page lists CC0, identifies the four recording creators, and relays the team's public-domain dedication. Its Prepared SFX Library.7z download link was followed directly.
sources.credit: Firearm recordings by Ben Jaszczak, Brian Nelson, Kevin Heras and Matthew Nanney. The Free Firearm Sound Library, CC0 1.0.

additionalSelections.description: The preserved master sheet identifies an AR-15/M4 5.56x45 report recorded at mid distance in front of the shooter, forward/back stereo. This supplies an actual mid-distance microphone recording for a distant-shot game cue. The source does not claim a specific far distance.
The preserved master sheet identifies an AK-47 7.62x39 single report recorded near the firearm in front of the shooter, left/right stereo.
additionalSelections.proposedUse: Distinct designed 7.62 rifle-report option for the fictional minigun. This is not an actual rotary minigun recording.

sources.title: Gun reload sounds
sources.evidence: The creator's OpenGameArt page lists CC0 and says the reloads were recorded with airsoft guns. Credit is optional. All three source download links were followed directly.
sources.credit: Reload and pump recordings by SpringySpringo. Gun reload sounds, CC0 1.0.

sources.title: Dry Fire
sources.credit: Dry Fire by brianhanson2nd, Freesound, CC0 1.0.
sources.evidence: The creator page identifies an actual Smith and Wesson 9 mm dry-fire recording, recorded with a Samson M10 microphone through an M-Audio MobilePre USB preamp, and lists Creative Commons 0. The public HQ MP3 preview URL was read directly from the page HTML.
sources.originalFormat: The page lists a 24-bit mono 44.1 kHz FLAC original. Original download requires login. Only the public HQ MP3 preview was acquired.

deliveryScope: Local candidate audio and audition files. No resource-pack pin, portal code, game firing system or live Minecraft state is changed.
auditoryReview: No listening or subjective sound-quality review has been performed by the assistant. Selection uses source identities, recorded metadata and measured waveforms.
